kata.name: memento roundtrip (c): version-skew restore of an old per-page snapshot into the new document shape - page-level fields drop and the collapsed pages are proven non-invertible
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the new shape has no page place, so page-level cells are named and the round trip proves the collapsed pages unrecoverable

expected.detail: the old per-page snapshot collapses onto the new document row; page_next, page_note and page_text have no place in the new shape and are named cell by cell
restore after save is not the identity: the collapse makes the smallest SnapshotPage element unrecoverable, and the proof names the element the candidate inverse returns instead

commands: python3 prototype/memento_roundtrip_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 4 faults, unique [0, 2, 2, 4] (baseline arm frozen)
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- migrate --json fixtures/katas/memento-roundtrip/restore-version-skew.ct.json  # exit 8, 5 lost_cell findings
cargo test -q -p catherine-ledger --test memento_roundtrip_kata version_skew  # ok: proof names SnapshotPage row 0; unique 4

comparison.conventional_baseline: A field-by-field save/restore checklist over sampled cells: it catches only the sampled page_text cells 0 and 1 because those rows are sampled and the field is null; it has no row-count or collapse model and cannot express restore-after-save identity.

procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/memento-roundtrip/README.md and faults.json before any run; the observed-results section was appended after the executed run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/memento_roundtrip_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: a field-by-field save/restore checklist over the pre-registered sample cells; --assert froze its detections.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real kernel: `catherine migrate --json` for the lost-data arm and `catherine_core::migrate::round_trip` in crates/catherine-ledger/tests/memento_roundtrip_kata.rs for the non-invertibility arm.
4. Elements were compared, not prose: lost_row:<object>#<row>, lost_cell:<arrow>#<row>, round_trip:<object>#<row>; an arm identifies an element only by naming it.

5. unique_detections = probe elements minus baseline-identified elements, re-derived by the frozen test; the verdict follows harness::derive_probe_verdict (empty unique = killed; unique + executed arm = survived).
